answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-cost. Every agent that wants to transact must lock a non-refundable bond; a thousand fake keys mean a thousand locks, so cost scales linearly while reward per identity collapses. To leave the wharf of newcomer status, an agent needs attestations from bonded peers whose own stake is slashed if they vouch for a ghost. Attacking becomes capital-bound: fakes need a real oasis of honest liquidity, and mimicking one costs more than any airdrop. Honest agents act as a beacon, publishing verifiable records that make cheap clusters visible.
